analysis.title: Meta's $628 Billion "Footnote": Count Zuck's Off-Balance Sheet Debt And The Stock Gets 35% More Expensive
key_insights: Needham (Laura Martin, Hold, no price target) argues off-balance sheet commitments belong in enterprise value. Adding them raises Meta's EV by 35%, Amazon's by 9% and Alphabet's by 3% on Needham's table.

Meta's off-balance sheet lines total roughly $628 billion against $112 billion of on-balance sheet debt and leases at the end of June, about 5.6x. The two lines are leases not yet commenced and non-cancelable contractual commitments.

Meta's Q2 10-Q shows about $278.99 billion of leases not yet commenced and $349.31 billion of non-cancelable commitments. July added about $68 billion of new data center leases after quarter-end, lifting the not-yet-commenced bucket by more than 10%.
On Needham's numbers Meta's EV/FY27E revenue moves from 6.15x to 8.32x.

Goldman credit strategy (Lynam) tracked $1.5 trillion of hyperscaler lease commitments after 2Q earnings, of which $1.0 trillion is uncommenced and not on the financial statements. Goldman expects AI-related issuers to keep trading with an extra spread risk premium.
Goldman's July 27 update had $1.2 trillion of lease commitments with $725 billion uncommenced, so the uncommenced total grew by roughly $275 billion in a few weeks.

Goldman (Crook) puts hyperscaler bond issuance at $250 billion this year versus under $20 billion in 2024, with $420 billion forecast for 2027 assuming 35% of capex is debt funded. The desk says hyperscalers do not care about the effect on long-end yields because interest expense is a small part of earnings.

Morgan Stanley's accounting team counted more than $3.1 trillion of off-balance sheet commitments in late August, adding Nvidia, Broadcom, guarantees and backstops. MS warns that variable interest entity treatment of structures such as Meta's Hyperion data center could change if residual value support becomes likely.
The article's own tracker puts hyperscaler off-balance sheet liabilities at $3.8 trillion as of Sept 30, up $700 billion from June 30. The article ties the pace of AI debt supply to rising yields.

The article says Needham books $0 of non-cancelable commitments for Amazon and Alphabet, although Alphabet's 10-Q discloses $707 billion of purchase commitments and Amazon's discloses $130 billion. Applied consistently, Alphabet's EV rises 21% and Amazon's 14%, and Alphabet's adjusted EV/FY27E revenue of 9.0x exceeds Meta's 8.3x.
The article puts Meta at roughly 42% EV uplift once the $68 billion July leases, the Hyperion and El Paso guarantees and the $14.7 billion contingent cloud deal are added.

Counterarguments are that purchase commitments are not debt in the conventional sense, the figures are undiscounted, and the market may price some of it already. MS notes Amazon and Google free cash flow turned negative in 2Q26 and Meta is expected to turn negative next quarter.
Needham's Hold thesis is mainly about strategy diffusion across custom chips, data centers, enterprise AI, agents, model APIs, compute sales and smart glasses, funded by $628 billion of commitments.
Goldman TMT specialists say Meta notched its best month since July 2013 on product momentum via Muse and now sits on the desk's overbought list.
Meta's 3Q 10-Q is due in late October and the article expects the off-balance sheet footnote to have grown.

market_movers.rationale: Needham keeps a Hold with no price target and argues Meta is more expensive than traditional EV multiples show once $626 billion of off-balance sheet obligations are added. It also cites strategy diffusion.

earnings_insights: Meta 2Q26 10-Q (reported, as of June 30, 2026): about $278.99 billion of leases not yet commenced and $349.31 billion of non-cancelable contractual commitments, with about $53.52 billion due in 2026 and $81.65 billion in 2027.
Meta 10-Q subsequent event: about $68 billion of additional data center leases signed in July 2026.
Morgan Stanley (estimate, via the article): Amazon and Google free cash flow turned negative in 2Q26 and Meta is expected to turn negative in 3Q26.
Meta's 3Q26 10-Q is due in late October 2026.
risk_factors: Off-balance sheet obligations at hyperscalers keep growing faster than the balance sheet, which raises effective leverage and future liquidity needs.
If supply and demand normalize ahead of expectations, companies may have to pay for excess capacity or renegotiate purchase contracts (Morgan Stanley).

Variable interest entity structures such as Meta's Hyperion venture could be consolidated if residual value support becomes likely (Morgan Stanley). Meta's 10-Q puts the residual value guarantee at roughly $28 billion.
Heavy hyperscaler debt supply could pressure long-end yields and widen spreads for AI-related issuers.
Meta free cash flow expected to turn negative in 3Q26 (Morgan Stanley).
Strategy diffusion at Meta across many AI and hardware initiatives (Needham).
charts_described: Needham table starts from traditional EV (market cap less cash plus on-balance sheet debt) and adds on-balance sheet leases, contracted leases not yet commenced and non-cancelable contractual commitments. For Meta the two off-balance sheet lines total about $628 billion against $112 billion on-balance sheet at end of June.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman TMT specialists place Meta on the desk's overbought list after its best month since July 2013.
cross_bank_references: Needham is the first equity analyst the article has seen to plug these commitments into a multiple, and the credit side got there first.
Morgan Stanley's off-balance sheet framing reads like a direct preview of Needham's argument.
Goldman credit strategy and Morgan Stanley both track hyperscaler lease and commitment totals, at $1.5 trillion and more than $3.1 trillion respectively.

tension_points.bull_case: Purchase commitments are contracts for servers, cloud capacity and chips that Meta expects to turn into revenue, so adding $350 billion of hardware orders is closer to capitalizing future capex than finding hidden debt. The figures are also undiscounted and the market may already price some of it.
tension_points.bear_case: Needham and Morgan Stanley say equity holders are residual claimants behind these obligations, and a commitment stops being not debt once the capacity is not wanted. Rating agencies already treat leases as debt, and the not-yet-commenced bucket grew by $68 billion in one month.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Morgan Stanley flags Meta free cash flow turning negative next quarter. Meta's 3Q 10-Q in late October showing a larger off-balance sheet total would support the bear side.

theme_stances.key_argument: Off-balance sheet leases and purchase commitments should be added to EV, which makes Meta materially more expensive than standard multiples show.
theme_stances.evidence: Using traditional EV calculations understates hyperscaler valuation multiples, we believe.

theme_stances.key_argument: Uncommenced lease commitments understate hyperscaler leverage and future liquidity needs, so AI-related issuers should carry extra spread.
theme_stances.evidence: We expect AI-related issuers will continue to trade with an additional spread risk premia.
